findings.title: traceID is no longer included in plugin request log output
findings.body: The previous implementation of `logRequest` explicitly extracted the traceID from the context via `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` and appended it to `logParams`. This code has been removed, and the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext` does not add traceID to the contextual logger attributes. As a result, the `traceID` field will no longer appear in 'Plugin Request Completed' log messages, which is a regression that reduces observability and makes it harder to correlate logs with traces.

findings.title: Adding `FromContext` to the `Logger` interface is a breaking change
findings.body: The `Logger` interface now requires a `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` method. Any external or third-party implementations of this interface (e.g., custom plugin loggers) will fail to compile after this change. Since the PR is described as a chore/rename, this silent interface expansion may surprise consumers. Consider whether this should be a separate interface or introduced with a deprecation/migration path.

findings.title: `NewMetricsMiddleware` returns a closure that mutates a shared `MetricsMiddleware` instance
findings.body: `NewMetricsMiddleware` creates a single `*MetricsMiddleware` and the returned `ClientMiddlewareFunc` mutates `imw.next` each time it is invoked. If this middleware is applied to multiple plugin clients (which is the typical case—one middleware chain per plugin), all clients share the same `MetricsMiddleware` and the `next` field will point to whichever client was wired last. This means requests for one plugin may be forwarded to the wrong next client. This is a pre-existing pattern from the old `InstrumentationMiddleware`, but it remains a correctness bug.

findings.title: Stream methods (`SubscribeStream`, `PublishStream`, `RunStream`) do not enrich the context
findings.body: The `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` does not call `instrumentContext` for `SubscribeStream`, `PublishStream`, or `RunStream`. If the `LoggerMiddleware` (or any downstream middleware) logs during these calls, the contextual logger will lack plugin/endpoint information. While this matches the previous behavior of the old `InstrumentationMiddleware`, it's worth noting as a gap now that contextual logging is explicitly separated into its own middleware.

findings.title: `TestLogger.FromContext` discards contextual attributes, making it impossible to test contextual logging
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` always returns a fresh `NewTestLogger()`, discarding any contextual attributes that were stored in the context. Tests that use `TestLogger` cannot verify that contextual attributes (pluginId, endpoint, etc.) are properly propagated through the middleware chain to the final log call. A test-capable implementation should capture or expose the contextual attributes for assertion.
